markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (99%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Conformal set holds only Normal, and all 5 similar cases agree [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal 99%, Benign 1% | Strongly favors Normal |
| Conformal set | {Normal} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / 36th percentile | Typical input |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 5 of 5 Normal | Unanimous |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 2, 7, 10) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; largest negative concept term · Unreliable
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 1, 6, 7) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; linked to lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Validated
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 8) · ↑ invasive · Slightly above typical; region 8 has highest risk (7%) · Validated
- **Tumor cell density** (regions 4, 8, 11) · context · 15 per mm², 9th percentile; few tumor nuclei sampled · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules is Unreliable (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Cell data cover regions 4, 8, 11 only, with too few tumor nuclei to judge.
- Region 8 shows a stromal-infiltration signal; a small invasive focus could be missed.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 8:** confirm whether the stroma is tumor-infiltrated; highest invasive risk (7%).
2. **Regions 4, 8, 11:** look for neoplastic nuclei; HoVer-Net found at most one each.
3. **Regions 2, 7, 10:** verify two-layered lobules by eye; that concept failed its spot check.
